In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}{e}^{y}) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}{e}^{y})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2x{e}^{y} & {x}^{2}{e}^{y}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x\text{ }\,{e}^{y})=2\text{ }\,{e}^{y}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}{e}^{y})=2x\text{ }\,{e}^{y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x\text{ }\,{e}^{y})=2x\text{ }\,{e}^{y}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}{e}^{y})={x}^{2}{e}^{y}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}2\text{ }\,{e}^{y} & 2x\text{ }\,{e}^{y} \\ 2x\text{ }\,{e}^{y} & {x}^{2}{e}^{y}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at $\left(1,0\right).$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(1,0)=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186157424 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-f2460b1b-0ae3-5791-81e8-e644fac55aa1"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id 17592186157001 :question/problem "Given that

![](images/5e/5ea286680d2cec429fe920628617d083f47dd53519c2d40f30115dee45a18bc3.svg)

The Hessian determinant $H(x,y)$ is the determinant of the second derivative:

$$
H(\mathbf x) = \det \left( \boldsymbol{f}''(\mathbf x) \right)
$$

In our case, we have

![](images/14/1488754e319066706880b21fd4642c7b6a75a458770cab254b974b13d35425a2.svg)

First, notice that since ![](images/c9/c92e0f35c58187af3fe961947e6e96f0cd82cf32bb00cfd4f51ca3c742339e0c.svg) we must have

$$
\dfrac{\partial f}{\partial x} = \ln y, 
\qquad 
\dfrac{\partial f}{\partial y} = \dfrac xy.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y)=0\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{x}{y})=\frac{1}{y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y)=\frac{1}{y}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{x}{y})=-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & \frac{1}{y} \\ \frac{1}{y} & -\frac{x}{{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Evaluating the second derivative at $(0,1),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(0,1)=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we have

$$
H(0,1) = 0 \cdot 0 - 1\cdot 1 = -1.
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "question-ed948579-cdd5-5155-941d-e802c724684f" :question/id #uuid "ed948579-cdd5-5155-941d-e802c724684f" :question/math-academy-id "q-163633" :question/problem "Find ${f}^{″}(-1,2)$ for the function $f(x,y)$ given that

$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since ${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}2xy+{y}^{2} & {x}^{2}+2xy\end{aligned}],$ 
 we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=2xy+{y}^{2},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}={x}^{2}+2xy.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2xy+{y}^{2})=2y\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+2xy)=2x+2y \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2xy+{y}^{2})=2x+2y\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+2xy)=2x\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}2y & 2x+2y \\ 2x+2y & 2x\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at $(-1,2).$ This gives

$$
{f}^{″}(-1,2)=[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-3dde31b2-4dff-5b09-bd6e-40098b2f0a7a"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id $$

$$

$$

First, notice that since ${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2} & -2y\end{aligned}],$ we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}={x}^{2},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=-2y.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2})=2x\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-2y)=0 \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2})=0\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-2y)=-2\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}2x & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-e0ef2dd1-71c9-595b-9973-83cddc9a73a6"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "Find ${f}^{″}(-\frac{\pi }{2},1)$ for the function $f(x,y)=y\operatorname{cos}⁡x.$" :question/worked-solution "For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, we compute the first derivative of $f(x,y),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(y\operatorname{cos}⁡x) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(y\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-y\operatorname{sin}⁡x & \operatorname{cos}⁡x\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-y\operatorname{sin}⁡x)=-y\operatorname{cos}⁡x\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)=-\operatorname{sin}⁡x \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-y\operatorname{sin}⁡x)=-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}-y\operatorname{cos}⁡x & -\operatorname{sin}⁡x \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡x & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at $(-\frac{\pi }{2},1).$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(-\frac{\pi }{2},1)=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-df98d6a0-0de7-5458-a3e0-290cebc7112b"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "Find ${f}^{″}(x,y)$ for the function $f(x,y)=x\operatorname{ln}⁡y-y.$" :question/worked-solution "For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, we compute the first derivative of $f(x,y),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\operatorname{ln}⁡y-y) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(x\operatorname{ln}⁡y-y)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & \frac{x}{y}-1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y)=0\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{x}{y}-1)=\frac{1}{y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y)=\frac{1}{y}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{x}{y}-1)=-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}0 & \frac{1}{y} \\ \frac{1}{y} & -\frac{x}{{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-eca99a2b-d50a-519b-aef0-e2b86f3c4cf7"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id evaluate the Hessian determinant of $f(x,y)$ at the point $(1,1).$" :question/worked-solution "For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

The Hessian determinant $H(x,y)$ is the determinant of the second derivative:

$$
H(x)=det({f}^{″}(x))
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since ${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}2x{y}^{3} & 3{x}^{2}{y}^{2}\end{aligned}],$ we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=2x{y}^{3},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=3{x}^{2}{y}^{2}.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x{y}^{3})=2{y}^{3}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(3{x}^{2}{y}^{2})=6x{y}^{2} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x{y}^{3})=6x{y}^{2}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(3{x}^{2}{y}^{2})=6{x}^{2}y\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2{y}^{3} & 6x{y}^{2} \\ 6x{y}^{2} & 6{x}^{2}y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Evaluating the second derivative at $(1,1),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(1,1)=[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 \\ 6 & 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we have

$$
H(1,1)=2\cdot 6-6\cdot 6=-24.
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186155673 :answer-field/correct 17592186155677 :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "question-f2460b1b-0ae3-5791-81e8-e644fac55aa1" :question/id #uuid "f2460b1b-0ae3-5791-81e8-e644fac55aa1" :question/math-academy-id "q-102692" :question/problem "Given that

evaluate the Hessian determinant of $f(x,y)$ at the point $(1,1).$" :question/worked-solution "For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

The Hessian determinant $H(x,y)$ is the determinant of the second derivative:

$$
H(x)=det({f}^{″}(x))
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{y}^{2}}{x} & 2y\operatorname{ln}⁡x\end{aligned}],$
we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=\frac{{y}^{2}}{x},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=2y\operatorname{ln}⁡x.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{{y}^{2}}{x})=-\frac{{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)=\frac{2y}{x} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{{y}^{2}}{x})=\frac{2y}{x}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)=2\operatorname{ln}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}} & \frac{2y}{x} \\ \frac{2y}{x} & 2\operatorname{ln}⁡x\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Evaluating the second derivative at $(1,1),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(1,1)=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we have

$$
H(1,1)=(-1)\cdot 0-2\cdot 2=-4.
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-57597420-75c9-5305-b6c7-82cc31ede092"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-57597420-75c9-5305-b6c7-82cc31ede092" :answer-field/id #uuid "57597420-75c9-5305-b6c7-82cc31ede092" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-3b6147f2-99cb-5e0e-bfe7-1ab9fcb4bfaf" :answer-field/choices ["answer-e1d3bd0b-8f50-5fda-8e7a-df552a252f05" "answer-3b6147f2-99cb-5e0e-bfe7-1ab9fcb4bfaf" "answer-4c3b39c3-ebcc-501e-bf32-f62c8ab6fbca" "answer-3bd5f2d0-f063-5f9a-8554-0e38b366ddee" "answer-9f8b4808-0307-5f43-b835-eaa5d7c78ac1"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-e1d3bd0b-8f50-5fda-8e7a-df552a252f05" :answer/id #uuid "e1d3bd0b-8f50-5fda-8e7a-df552a252f05" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-2" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-3b6147f2-99cb-5e0e-bfe7-1ab9fcb4bfaf" :answer/id #uuid "3b6147f2-99cb-5e0e-bfe7-1ab9fcb4bfaf" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-4" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-4c3b39c3-ebcc-501e-bf32-f62c8ab6fbca" :answer/id #uuid "4c3b39c3-ebcc-501e-bf32-f62c8ab6fbca" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-6" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-3bd5f2d0-f063-5f9a-8554-0e38b366ddee" :answer/id #uuid "3bd5f2d0-f063-5f9a-8554-0e38b366ddee" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "3" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-9f8b4808-0307-5f43-b835-eaa5d7c78ac1" :answer/id #uuid "9f8b4808-0307-5f43-b835-eaa5d7c78ac1" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "5" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186158568 :tutorial/content "We've seen how to calculate the total derivative of a function $f: \mathbb R^n \to \mathbb R.$ In this lesson, we will learn how to calculate its second derivative.

For a function $f: \mathbb R^n \to \mathbb R,$ given by

![](images/44/44a95860d7e7bd926f4d94c2ebb5b037e8537ac622f7c86b500aa06b9f959250.svg)

the total derivative of $f$ is given by the matrix

![](images/e0/e0c9f72b67a531f992342e9f9e0b74f447de5e2b62c9fd81f08804096a912e67.svg)

To differentiate $f$ once more, we first need to take the transpose of the first derivative:

![](images/4d/4d23282171c39149eeebd7301550ebdf1727b86736a57de6e5d7b6ea96891157.svg)

To calculate the **second derivative** of $f,$ we simply apply the definition of the total derivative to $\left(\boldsymbol f'(\mathbf x)\right)^T.$ By doing this, we get the following $n\times n$ matrix:

![](images/3d/3d62db0c4018fcce47077285aa05e6c4ea3c79e972ab87fccf5165a07083eda9.svg)

Notice that this matrix is *symmetric* due to the equality of mixed partial derivatives. This becomes important later. 

The matrix $\boldsymbol{f}''(\mathbf x)$ is sometimes called the **Hessian matrix,** and its determinant, 

$$
H(\mathbf x) = \det\big( \boldsymbol{f}''(\mathbf x) \big)
$$

is called the **Hessian determinant**.

Note that in the case of a two-variable function $f(x,y),$ the second derivative is given by

![](images/e8/e83195902ce2cdc2e0ff6c1f51ebc679a4bddd51fedd38c4bc6fddc4c73373dd.svg)

In this lesson, we'll primarily focus on two-variable functions $f(x,y).$ However, we should remember that the techniques discussed here can be applied to scalar functions with an arbitrary number of variables." :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186157481 :activity/expected-seconds 660.0 :db/ensure [:activity/validate]}]

evaluate the Hessian determinant of $f(x,y)$ at the point $(1,1).$" :question/worked-solution "For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

The Hessian determinant $H(x,y)$ is the determinant of the second derivative:

$$
H(x)=det({f}^{″}(x))
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since ${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}2x{y}^{3} & 3{x}^{2}{y}^{2}\end{aligned}],$ we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=2x{y}^{3},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=3{x}^{2}{y}^{2}.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x{y}^{3})=2{y}^{3}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(3{x}^{2}{y}^{2})=6x{y}^{2} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x{y}^{3})=6x{y}^{2}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(3{x}^{2}{y}^{2})=6{x}^{2}y\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2{y}^{3} & 6x{y}^{2} \\ 6x{y}^{2} & 6{x}^{2}y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Evaluating the second derivative at $(1,1),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(1,1)=[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 \\ 6 & 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we have

$$
H(1,1)=2\cdot 6-6\cdot 6=-24.
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186155673 :answer-field/correct 17592186155677 :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "question-f2460b1b-0ae3-5791-81e8-e644fac55aa1" :question/id #uuid "f2460b1b-0ae3-5791-81e8-e644fac55aa1" :question/math-academy-id "q-102692" :question/problem "Given that

$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$

The Hessian determinant $H(x,y)$ is the determinant of the second derivative:

$$
H(x)=det({f}^{″}(x))

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].

${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{y}^{2}}{x} & 2y\operatorname{ln}⁡x\end{aligned}],$

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=\frac{{y}^{2}}{x},\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=2y\operatorname{ln}⁡x.
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{{y}^{2}}{x})=-\frac{{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)=\frac{2y}{x} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{{y}^{2}}{x})=\frac{2y}{x}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)=2\operatorname{ln}⁡x\end{aligned}

$$

$$

Finally, we have

$$
H(1,1)=(-1)\cdot 0-2\cdot 2=-4.

![](images/22/22dd960829ea268e5aade685b56949f8998f87ae8c040a90f04436cbfc6b9a58.png)

![](images/4f/4fede2bb5c2306f62b55b7996488baee52c69e7d41b011e0e9d2b7405e63a8f4.png)

First, we compute the first derivative of $f(x,y),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}{e}^{y}) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}{e}^{y})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2x{e}^{y} & {x}^{2}{e}^{y}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x\text{ }\,{e}^{y})=2\text{ }\,{e}^{y}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}{e}^{y})=2x\text{ }\,{e}^{y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x\text{ }\,{e}^{y})=2x\text{ }\,{e}^{y}\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}{e}^{y})={x}^{2}{e}^{y}\end{aligned}

$$

For a function $f: \mathbb R^n \to \mathbb R,$ given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]
$$

the total derivative of $f$ is given by the matrix

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}]
$$

To differentiate $f$ once more, we first need to take the transpose of the first derivative:

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{1}} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{2}} \\ ⋮ \\ \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}]
$$

To calculate the **second derivative** of $f,$ we simply apply the definition of the total derivative to $\left(\boldsymbol f'(\mathbf x)\right)^T.$ By doing this, we get the following $n\times n$ matrix:

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}]
$$

Notice that this matrix is *symmetric* due to the equality of mixed partial derivatives. This becomes important later. 

The matrix $\boldsymbol{f}''(\mathbf x)$ is sometimes called the **Hessian matrix,** and its determinant, 

$$
H(\mathbf x) = \det\big( \boldsymbol{f}''(\mathbf x) \big)
$$

is called the **Hessian determinant**.

Note that in the case of a two-variable function $f(x,y),$ the second derivative is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}]
$$

In this lesson, we'll primarily focus on two-variable functions $f(x,y).$ However, we should remember that the techniques discussed here can be applied to scalar functions with an arbitrary number of $$

the total derivative of $f$ is given by the matrix

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}]
$$

To differentiate $f$ once more, we first need to take the transpose of the first derivative:

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{1}} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{2}} \\ ⋮ \\ \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}]
$$

To calculate the **second derivative** of $f,$ we simply apply the definition of the total derivative to $\left(\boldsymbol f'(\mathbf x)\right)^T.$ By doing this, we get the following $n\times n$ matrix:

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}]
$$

Notice that this matrix is *symmetric* due to the equality of mixed partial derivatives. This becomes important later. 

The matrix $\boldsymbol{f}''(\mathbf x)$ is sometimes called the **Hessian matrix,** and its determinant, 

$$
H(\mathbf x) = \det\big( \boldsymbol{f}''(\mathbf x) \big)
$$

is called the **Hessian determinant**.

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}]
